task_context: A public Qwen3-8B GSM8K adapter (MetaMathQA, author reports 0.84 in bf16 with vLLM) drops Qwen's official Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M from 0.945 to 0.425 on GSM8K, with stuttering outputs. available_skills: adapter applied at runtime or merged
re-conversion from the published checkpoint at Q4_K_M, Q4_0, Q5_K_M, Q6_K and Q8_0
CPU versus CUDA backend
transformers + PEFT on 4-bit NF4
norm-weight comparison with the source checkpoint
proposed_action: Hold the adapter and 100 GSM8K items fixed and vary only the base weights file: official Q4_K_M, official Q8_0, our own Q4_K_M converted from the published checkpoint, other quant types, and a PEFT/NF4 reference; then compare a norm tensor with the source weights.
observed_outcome: The official Q4_K_M scored 0.37 (0.47 on CPU only), the official Q8_0 0.87, our own Q4_K_M from the published weights 0.86 and the PEFT/NF4 reference 0.85 against the author's 0.84. Only the official Q4_K_M fails, on both backends; its RMSNorm weights differ from the published model's by 20-55% because it was converted from an AWQ-rescaled checkpoint, so the adapter lands in the wrong weight basis. Small self-distilled adapters barely moved the official file, long-trained ones broke it.
verification_method: Check general.name and general.finetune, or compare a norm tensor against the source weights, before attaching a LoRA to a downloaded GGUF; or convert the GGUF yourself from the checkpoint the adapter was trained on.
